answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs therefore has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator burns authoring per alias. Because the ocean hash is checked against the bridge checkpoint at intake, the mesa audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. Scaling to 832 identities multiplies that fee by 319 with no matching gain in influence. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
